maya: quick heads-up — FP8 kernel enablement (H100 + L40S) in the long-run smoke found a small consistent generation drift on orion-13b when using AWQ fallback + mixed GPTQ shards. attaching minimal logs below. :eyes:

maya: log excerpt:
```
# baseline (fp16): "The quick brown fox jumped over the lazy dog and then..."
# fp8-enabled: "The quick brown fox jumps above the lazy dog and then..."
# delta: semantically same but phrasing skew across several seeds, ppl delta ~ +0.7
# canary summary: 4800 inferences, 34 flagged diffs (~0.71%), top tokens with shifted prob mass: 'over'->'above'
```

sam: which exact artifact + reproducer? h100 or l40s only? batch/seq?

maya: both. ran on h100 farm and L40S nightly. command: 
```
rdw run --model orion-13b --quant awq --precision fp8 --batch 1 --seq 2048 --profile longrun --seed 42 --kv-tiling true --runqueue 16
```

sam: thanks — can you paste the kernel flags envs? sometimes runqueue + tiling + packing cause tiny reorderings.

maya: envs used: `REDWOOD_FP8_ENABLE=1 REDWOOD_PRECISION_HANDSHAKE=auto REDWOOD_KV_TILING=1 REDWOOD_RUNQUEUE=16 REDWOOD_FP8_AUTOSCALE=1`

jonah: i've seen a similar signal before — it's usually at the attention rescale handshake between fp8 staging and fp16 accumulation. the resumable fallback path occasionally uses a slightly different rounding path. try REDWOOD_FP8_AUTOSCALE=0 or handshake=per-layer to see if it flips. also shadow-run with linear-prefetch disabled.

priya: agree. for bisect i usually run per-layer precision overrides to find first offending layer. small repro (python):
```
from redwood import Client
cli = Client()
for l in range(0, 40):
    cli.set_layer_precision("orion-13b", layer=l, precision="fp16")
    out = cli.generate("The quick brown fox", seed=42, seq=512)
    print(l, out[:80])
```
This isolates whether it's qkv/mha/residual.

maya: ran the bisect overnight on L40S. first suspicious layer 9 (attention projection). lowering handshake to per-layer made diffs disappear in the short-run but reappeared after ~10k tokens. attached short tail: 
```
[2026-03-18T03:12:44Z] layer9: accumulated scale drift 1.0007 -> 1.0013 after 12k steps
[2026-03-18T03:12:46Z] sample mismatch rate: 0.9%
```

sam: that suggests numeric accumulation fog rather than pure quant table mismatch. try `REDWOOD_ACCUM_CLIP=1e3` and `REDWOOD_SCALE_SMOOTH=0.99` to stabilize. also test with `PRECISION_SWAP=fp8->int8` to see if AWQ routing changes behaviour.

ci-bot: shadow-traffic summary: 120 requests run over canary pool, 2.3% flagged quality regression vs baseline, 0 NaNs recorded, 4 tail-timeouts. see /canary/reports/5055556789. :robot_face:

jonah: if shadow shows no NaNs but quality drift, it's a subtle bias. one experiment that helped before: force per-channel quant scales for the attention q/k/v weights (instead of per-tensor). AWQ default is per-tensor on this model; try `QUANT_PER_CHANNEL=1` and rerun.

priya: also compare GPTQ shards vs AWQ shards independently — mixing them in the runtime sometimes triggers alternate kernel paths. run three combos: (AWQ-only), (GPTQ-only), (AWQ-gptq-mix) and collect token-level KL. small script: run 1k prompts, compute avg KL and top-10 token shifts.

maya: did AWQ-only vs GPTQ-only quick run: AWQ-only KL +0.45, GPTQ-only KL +0.12, mixed KL +0.68. mixed is worst. logs show different kernel selection: AWQ path uses kernel_v3_handshake, GPTQ uses kernel_v2_accum.

sam: that kernel swap is the smoking gun. need kernel-level traces. @eng-runtime can we enable tracepoints for handshake entry/exit and scale updates?

priya: opened trace ticket RT-1209 and attached sample memtrace. suggestion: instrument `attention_rescale()` to log pre/post scale and rounding mode. keep sampling low — heavy trace affects perf.

maya: action items I can take: 1) run per-channel quant + handshake=per-layer on both hardware pools 2) collect kernel traces for offending window 3) run longer shadow at lower qps to reproduce persistent reappearance.

jonah: i'll schedule a short kernel debug slot on thursday with eng-runtime. bring a minimal repro and the bisect output. add the per-layer override script and both hardware jobs.

sam: one more thought — try disabling KV prefetch fusion on L40S. we've had small reorderings from prefetch packaging before. `REDWOOD_PREFETCH_FUSION=0`.

maya: ok doing a coordinated run now (L40S prefusion off, per-channel quant, handshake per-layer, autopscale=0). will post results. thanks all. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: note: canary alert created (#canary-5055556789) — assign eng-runtime if regression persists.

maya: update (last run): after per-channel + handshake per-layer + autopscale=0, KL dropped to +0.08 and sample mismatch down to 0.12% on L40S (10k samples). H100 still shows ~0.3% with same flags — different kernel codepath on H100. next step: kernel trace on H100.

priya: excellent progress. record these as experiments in the quant-bakeoff doc: /docs/quant-bakeoffs/2026-03-fp8-h100-l40s-mixedpath.md and label runs with metadata: hw=L40S/H100, quant=(awq,gptq,mix), handshake=(auto/per-layer), per_channel=(0/1).

maya: will do. closing loop tomorrow after kernel traces. :sleeping:
